whatTheyArgued: Koopman (PNAS 17(5), 1931), read on disk: for a Hamiltonian system (more generally a steady flow of a fluid of positive density, with an invariant positive integral) the flow S_t acts on complex-valued functions of state by U_t g(A) = g(S_t A); on a Hilbert space of such functions U_t is a LINEAR, UNITARY operator even though the dynamics is nonlinear. That is the move: nonlinear dynamics becomes linear action on observables, which brings Hilbert-space spectral theory to classical mechanics. Because U_t is unitary the eigenvalues lie on the unit circle: pure frequency, no growth or decay. Growth and decay appear in later generalizations (Mezic and co-workers), not in the 1931 note. DMD (Schmid 2010, J. Fluid Mech.) is a data algorithm whose eigenvalues can approximate the Koopman spectrum under conditions.

scholarship.ref: Brunton, Budisic, Kaiser, Kutz, 'Modern Koopman Theory for Dynamical Systems', SIAM Review (2022), abstract read
scholarship.supports: Koopman operator is an infinite-dimensional linear operator on measurement functions representing nonlinear dynamics; DMD is one of the numerical algorithms built on it
scholarship.disputes: finite-dimensional embeddings in which dynamics appear linear are described as a central open problem; DMD eigenvalues approximate Koopman eigenvalues only under assumptions (I read only the abstract)

ourUse: dmd.js: SVD-based Dynamic Mode Decomposition of a state trajectory; returns complex eigenvalues with magnitude, growth = log|lambda|/dt, and frequency (argument). The header states DMD eigenvalues approximate Koopman eigenvalues and that the Hilbert-space structure is 'measured rather than asserted'.

bends.ours: Compendium credit: 'modes with growth and frequency (1931; DMD, 2010)'.
bends.theirs: The 1931 operator is unitary, so its modes have frequency only. Growth comes from later work and from DMD on dissipative or finite data; the date range in the credit puts both in one name.

bends.ours: 'the operator whose eigenvalues DMD approximates' stated flatly; a finite-sample DMD of a short text trajectory.
bends.theirs: DMD approximates Koopman spectra only under conditions (observable richness, sufficient data). Our use is a finite linear fit; calling its modes Koopman modes is conditional, and the file does not check the conditions.

bends.ours: File head, in Koopman's voice: 'My teaching, however, emphasizes the importance of understanding the underlying mathematical principles ...'.
bends.theirs: Koopman wrote no such sentence; it is model-written text in the author's first person.

bends.ours: 'the spectral face of a stream' (a text or event trajectory).
bends.theirs: Koopman's setting is a measure-preserving deterministic flow on a state space; applying it to a symbolic stream is our analogy.
